source_evidence.location: Exact Met object page Artwork Details and Overview; Overview first paragraph: Johnson as earliest known professional African American painter | Overview opening paragraph: Edith Halpert discovery in late 1950s
source_evidence.finding: Met Overview identifies the sitter as Emma Van Name, painted circa 1805 by Joshua Johnson. Johnson is described as the earliest known professional African American painter; artwork discovered by art dealer Edith Halpert in the late 1950s and later exhibited widely. Colors, compositional complexity and meticulous detailing make this an outstanding child portrait.
